title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 87
paragraphs: When Leotychides had finished speaking and the Athenians still would not listen to him, he went back home. The Aeginetans, before paying the penalty for their earlier wrongs — when to please the Thebans they had offered insult to the Athenians — now acted as follows. Resentful of the Athenians' behavior and believing themselves wronged, they made preparations to avenge themselves. While the Athenians were celebrating their four-yearly festival at Sunion, the Aeginetans lay in wait for the sacred ship that was being sent to the festival, seized it — it was full of the leading men of Athens — and, having captured it, threw the men in chains.
